author: root/coordinator

checks.description: Synthetic candidate admission requires exact expected/live CID plus existing controller/type/capacity conditions and refuses missing, malformed, mismatched or ambiguous candidates.
All identity failures happen before any block-node open, and untrusted network job input cannot override the expected CID.
The read-only diagnostic and production SD/NFS builder remain unchanged and contain no writer or private CID.
Focused native/static ARM64 and existing locator/SD-NFS regression tests plus workflow/document checks pass with synthetic-only limits recorded.

constraints.text: Require a complete, canonical 32-hex-character CID from both trusted expected configuration and live sysfs; reject missing, malformed, or mismatched values and any ambiguous MMC inventory.

Keep the expected CID outside network job fields and repository fixtures. Prove every identity refusal precedes block-node open; record that path-to-opened-device binding remains for later writer integration.
Do not add the helper or any writer, trigger, private CID, or CID provisioning mechanism to the production SD/NFS image or change the existing read-only probe or boot policy.

Use synthetic identifiers only, run the named offline tests and hash/document checks, and report the limited evidence level and unresolved live CID comparison under H12. This approval grants no physical action or release authority.

decision.rationale: The existing locator admits a controller/type/capacity candidate but explicitly lacks unique module identity. H10 did not record a CID, the later private CID has not been compared with the live card, and the QEMU writer uses a synthetic USB target. Adding synthetic CID admission before target open is a bounded improvement within decision 0018 and advances the writerless goal. The proposal keeps H12 as the single physical gate and does not change production imaging, boot policy, or hardware authority. This approval covers offline test sources only; synthetic matching cannot prove the installed printer module is safe to write.

evidence.limitations: Synthetic fixtures only. The pinned printer kernel has not been checked, no live CID was read, and no block device or printer was accessed.
evidence.method: Ran the synthetic sysfs C fixture through the native and static ARM64 test harness. Exact fake CID and current locator controller/type/capacity criteria admit; missing/malformed/wrong-case/mismatched CID and absent, wrong-type, wrong-capacity, or multiple MMC candidates refuse.
evidence.profile: test-sv08-01 controller/capacity shape with synthetic CID values

evidence.limitations: This proves callback ordering in a synthetic fixture, not the eventual writer's block-device open binding or end-to-end network descriptor handling.
evidence.method: Open-spy callback remains at zero for every refusal and runs once only after a matching admission. The API accepts expected CID separately and has no network-job parameter; this task contains no descriptor parser or path-to-opened-device binding.

evidence.limitations: No fresh image composition or target-kernel integration was performed; no private CID, writer, trigger, or boot-policy change is included.
evidence.method: Compared the submitted diff and source hashes: the test-only helper/fixture and regression test are added; existing read-only init.c and production image builder are unchanged. The helper is not included in the production image build.

evidence.limitations: Offline synthetic only. The CID expected-value provisioning source, match to the live printer, identity-to-opened-device binding, physical write and printer boot remain unvalidated; H12 is still required.
evidence.method: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_sd_network_cid_admission tests.test_sd_network_env_probe tests.test_sd_network_image -q` passed 13 tests; `python3 -m py_compile tests/test_sd_network_cid_admission.py`, static ARM64 `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` compile, local Markdown target check and `git diff --check` passed. Feature-workflow validation is run at integration.

tasks.title: Implement and verify synthetic CID-bound eMMC target admission

verification.rationale: Checks nca-01 through nca-04 pass at clean source commit 71320a888fe95c57c3291bf9b3bb6c674d0962e3 within their approved offline synthetic scope. Exact lowercase 32-character expected and live CIDs, existing controller/type/capacity and unique MMC inventory gate the callback; missing, malformed, mismatched and ambiguous fixtures refuse before target-open. The API takes expected CID separately and has no network-job parameter; descriptor parsing and trusted provisioning are outside this slice. Production init.c and SD/NFS builder are unchanged. Native tests and static AArch64 compilation pass (13 tests total); the pinned upstream Linux source citation supports the format while printer-kernel behavior remains unverified. The submitted evidence and complete diff are bound to clean HEAD. Path-to-opened-device identity, live CID comparison, writer integration and physical use remain unvalidated under H12.
